name: Dollar Industries Ltd
title: Dollar Industries Ltd - 541403 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Dollar Industries Q1 FY27: margin up on a 4-5% price hike, but volume fell 1.6% and management is protecting margin over share, with FY27 guidance of 11-13% growth and 11.5-12.5% EBITDA margin.

summary.headline: Dollar Industries Q1 FY27: operating EBITDA up 11.4% to INR 48 crore at 11.8% margin, on price hikes and no discounting, while volume fell 1.6%.
summary.overview: Operating income rose 1.4% YoY to INR 405 crore, with gross margin up 192 bps to 37.4% after a 4-5% calibrated price increase taken in April. Management chose not to match market discounting, so revenue growth was limited and volume declined 1.6% YoY, mainly from Dollar Man. PAT rose 22.1% to INR 26 crore and net debt fell to INR 192 crore from INR 277 crore at March 2026. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 11-13% and operating EBITDA margin of 11.5-12.5%.

financial_highlights.value: INR 192 crore (Net debt/equity 0.20x; net debt/operating EBITDA 1.01x)

segments.name: Dollar Always (economic)
segments.commentary: 44% of revenue; volume flat YoY; ASP up from INR 47 to INR 49 after price hike.

segments.name: Dollar Man (incl. Big Boss)
segments.commentary: 38% of revenue; volume down around 3-3.5% YoY, the main driver of the overall volume decline; ASP up from INR 82 to INR 85.

segments.name: Dollar Woman (Missy)
segments.commentary: About 8% of revenue; volume up 1.5-2% YoY; ASP up from INR 100 to INR 104.

segments.name: Dollar Protect (rainwear)
segments.commentary: 5.6% of revenue; value growth 49% and volume growth 68% YoY.

segments.name: Force NXT (premium)
segments.commentary: About 4% of revenue in Q1; volume up 7% YoY but value declined on lower ASP as innerwear mix rose; overall ASP about INR 220. FY26 base INR 85-90 crore (4.5% of sales).

segments.name: Socks
segments.commentary: About 2% of sales; volume down around 7% YoY.

segments.name: Quick commerce channel
segments.commentary: 5% of revenue (vs 3.1% in Q1 FY26); value growth 59.4%, volume growth 15.1% YoY.

segments.name: E-commerce channel
segments.commentary: About 4.5% of sales per management; total e-commerce including quick commerce about 10%.

segments.name: South region
segments.commentary: Value growth 22.9%, volume growth 7.3% YoY; 8.9% of revenue vs 7.2% in Q1 FY26.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: INR 19 crore revenue across 15 countries; value growth 16.2%, volume growth 15.5% YoY; 4.9% of revenue vs 4.2%.

segments.name: G.O.A.T (JV, D2C)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue INR 16.44 crore (+21% YoY), PAT INR 2.27 crore (13.8% margin); FY26 revenue about INR 50 crore, FY27 target INR 75 crore (management also cited 25-30% growth).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 11-13% (in one answer, a 'target of 12-13%' was cited for the ad-cost math; the internal target was described as 11-12%).
FY27 operating EBITDA margin guided at 11.5-12.5%.
Management expects the industry pricing and discounting to stabilise over the next one to two quarters.
Ad spend capped at INR 100 crore annually; ad cost expected to fall to about 5% of sales from 5.5% last year, a ~0.5% margin benefit if growth target is met.
Cash conversion cycle to fall 6-7 days vs March 2026 in FY27 and by 15-18 days over three years; target 130-135 days in three to four years.
Debt target: total debt to zero by FY28; INR 86 crore repaid in Q1 alone. No major capex commitments near term.
Lakshya Phase-2 under way to raise active retailers from about 80,000 towards 90,000 in FY27; no new states entered for now.
Force NXT expected to grow 20-25% YoY over the next 2-3 years; G.O.A.T JV targeted at INR 75 crore in FY27.
capex_capacity: No major capital expenditure commitment in the near term; capital allocation focus is free cash flow and debt reduction.
Project Lakshya: 327 distributors across 14 states as of June 2026, contributing 31% of business in Q1 FY27 (about 20-22% of distributors enrolled).
Enrolled retailers about 1,73,561 vs about 80,000 active; Phase-2 targets reactivating about 1 lakh inactive retailers.
No new states are being enrolled in Lakshya because each rollout disrupts the state for 5-6 months; UP and other large states remain unenrolled for now.
Force NXT D2C website being built, with agencies in talks; innerwear (bamboo and modal) and activewear launched under the brand.
demand_pricing: Price hikes of 4-5% taken in April 2026 across all brands; management says no further hike is planned as yarn and cotton prices have stabilised.
Volume decline attributed to customer scepticism after the price hike and intense competitor deep discounting; management chose not to match discounts.
Management says low-cost inventory contributed only a small part of the margin gain, since input prices began rising from late February.
Lakshya distributors' ROI is 17-24%; receivable days are better in Lakshya states than in non-Lakshya states.
Management noted the industry-wide price discipline is improving; Q1 volume decline was the main concern raised by analysts.

qa_highlights.question: Is quick commerce growth broad-based across products, and what drove the South region's strong growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed South growth to the Mahesh Babu brand association (signed about two years ago) plus better retailer placement and rising consumer acceptance. Quick commerce was about 5% of sales, growing 59% in value in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the industry price hike sustainable, and will the volume decline be recovered in the next three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects pricing and discounting to stabilise over one to two quarters. It targets double-digit volume-plus-value growth for FY27, with full-year revenue growth of about 11-12% internally and 11-13% guided.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion, and can it be sustained without further price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Two drivers: the 4-5% price hike and not matching competitor discounts, which held revenue growth to about 1.5%. Management said low-cost inventory was a small contributor, as input prices rose from late February and the hike came in April. It sees no further hike needed as yarn and cotton have stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments drove the volume decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Dollar Man volume fell about 3-3.5%, the main driver of the total 1.6% volume decline. Socks fell about 7% but are only about 2% of sales. Dollar Woman grew 1.5-2% in volume and Dollar Always was flat YoY.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin benefit will come from the INR 100 crore advertising cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Ad spend was 7.7% of revenue in Q1. Management expects ad cost to fall to about 5% of sales from 5.5% last year at the 11-13% growth target, a benefit of about 0.5% of margin. Ad spend breakdown: about INR 100-102 crore a year across digital, TV, IPL, hoardings and in-store branding.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Lakshya Phase-2 mechanics, and why are no new states being added?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase-2 reactivates retailers, not distributors: 1,73,561 enrolled against about 80,000 active, with a target of about 90,000 active in FY27. No new states are being enrolled because each rollout disrupts a state for 5-6 months; UP and other large states remain for later.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cash conversion cycle and debt targets?
qa_highlights.answer: The CCC is 160 days; management targets a 6-7 day cut in FY27 vs March 2026 and 15-18 days over three years, reaching 130-135 days in three to four years. INR 86 crore of debt was repaid in Q1, and total debt (about 90% working capital) is targeted at zero by FY28. Q1 operating cash flow was about INR 96 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Force NXT and the G.O.A.T JV?
qa_highlights.answer: Force NXT grew about 7% in volume in Q1, but value declined as innerwear with lower ASP grew. Overall ASP is about INR 220. FY26 revenue was INR 85-90 crore (4.5% of sales), with 20-25% growth expected for the next 2-3 years. G.O.A.T's FY27 target is INR 75 crore, against about INR 50 crore in FY26.

risks_watch: Volume trajectory: Q1 volume fell 1.6% YoY, mainly Dollar Man (down about 3-3.5%). Management's double-digit volume recovery target for FY27 is a key test.
Pricing discipline: management expects industry discounting to stabilise in one to two quarters. Continued deep discounting by competitors could pressure volume or margins.
Raw material costs: yarn and cotton are described as stabilised, with no further hike planned. Management's view that margins hold at 11-12% depends on this.
Lakshya Phase-2 execution: active retailers need to rise from about 80,000 toward about 90,000 in FY27. No new states are being enrolled, and UP and other large states remain unenrolled.

Working capital and debt: CCC of 160 days and debtor days (target 85-90) must improve as planned. Zero total debt by FY28 depends on cash flow, and management said about 90% of debt is working capital.
key_quotes: This improvement was supported by the calibrated price increase implemented during the quarter which we had flagged in our previous call, and it is encouraging to see it translate into healthier realizations and stronger margins.

And we are still didn't give in to the market in terms of extra discounting and the schemes that are going on and try to protect our margin and operating cash flow as well, because of which, yes, we were unable to garner 9% or 10% kind of revenue growth.
So, currently, we are standing at somewhere around 160 days.
Yes, already we repaid around INR 86 crores in this quarter only.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, pricing and the balance sheet, but more cautious on volume, which management attributed to customer scepticism after the price hike and competitor discounting. Answers on pricing stabilisation and volume recovery were framed as hopes or internal targets rather than firm commitments.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 11-13% (midpoint 12%) and EBITDA margin 11.5-12.5%, but backing is price hikes, Lakshya retailer expansion and small new lines with no specific capacity or order numbers; volume fell 1.6% in Q1 and no capacity additions or major capex are planned.
